newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest blasts linked to organised crime - police.
newsitem.headline: Budapest blasts linked to organised crime - police.

text.p: Grenade attacks damaged property in Budapest at the weekend in the latest of a rash of explosions in Hungary and police said they bore the hallmarks of organised crime.

Two hand grenades early on Monday blew out the windows of a car showroom and a small restaurant without causing injuries, while on Saturday another grenade attack damaged a luxury car belonging to a gambling machine operator.
"Both explosions were some sort of warning and show strong indications that they were linked to organised crime," National police spokesman Laszlo Garamvolgyi told Reuters.
Hungary has been hit by a rash of bombings this year, which have so far caused material damage but no casualties.
Earlier this month a small bomb exploded in a dustbin near Budapest's Synagogue, the largest in Europe.
As of mid-October, the Hungarian press reported that police were investigating 13 explosions of hand grenades and other devices this year, compared to 28 blasts in the preceding seven years.
Police have said they have no evidence of terrorist groups operating in the country.
